_doc: Weather (Atmosphere, src/tactical/view/atmosphere.gd; its rules effects: Weather, src/tactical/weather.gd). One mood per gig, picked from the gig's seed and weighted by its district (data/world/city.json), kept on the gig as `mood` like its day/night `sky`, so a save reloads the same. Every gig with sky over it has one (no_sky_scenes: the undercity's tunnels and the arcology's atrium have none). ODDS: the official Night City Weather supplement (R. Talsorian free DLC, 2021; collected in Interface RED vol. 2; cited `NCW p.N`) is the only source that gives odds: per in-game month a 1d6 Current Conditions roll on one of four seasonal tables (NCW p.3), and on a 6 a 1d10 Strange Weather roll (NCW p.3). The campaign has no calendar, so the base weights are the year-round average of the four seasonal tables (HOUSE-RULE: each season a quarter of the year), in 1/1440ths: clear 6/24, overcast 7/24, light rain 5/24, heavy rain 2/24, each Strange Weather row 1/60 (row 8, cold snap or heat wave by the Temperature roll: cold snap in the 11 of 24 season-rolls that come up Cold or Cool). Rerolling into Strange Weather mid-gig is the Weather Turns twist (Twist fx weather). District leanings (region, profile, look tags, district by id: added to the base) are ours, each with its reason in `_why`. MECHANICS (NCW p.4-5, all 'at the GM's discretion', so kept behind data): `sight` is the penalty to Perception checks to see and to ranged attacks at a target past the first range band, out under the open sky (Weather.sight_penalty); `heat` raises an existing armor penalty to REF, DEX and MOVE (Combatant.heat); `outage` is a Utility Code outage the mood brings (blackout: power). `effects` false turns every mechanic off. LOOK: night / day blocks override the mood's own keys by day or night. Air over the scene (greybox scene_look): tower bands take fog / fog_d / fog_h / fog_hd / sky / smog; every other map the fog colour and sky and its own fog density scaled by fog_k (never the post palette, never ambient, key, rim or lamp light: owner). Tower dressing (TowerDress): cast + cast_k (far city), glow + grid (street grid), lit [a, b] (smog's under-light), thick (smog layers), wet (facade sheen), rain / rain_col, dust / dust_col round the tower. The play area (WeatherFx, over open-sky squares only, hidden under roofs and with the cutaway): rain (density) / rain_col / rain_len (m) / rain_speed (m/s) / slant (m across per m fallen), flakes / flake_col / flake_size / flake_fall (ash, ice glints), motes / mote_col / wind (m/s, blown dust), glow (motes and flakes glow: radioactive), haze / haze_col (low drifting haze over the open ground, lit by the neon), wet (ground sheen and puddles: outdoor ground only), ice (frosted ground, glassy puddles), flood (standing water), lightning (flashes a minute: the sky, the wet ground and the rain light up, never the play area's lamps). Player-facing text (name, hud) never cites a page.
twist_why: Weather Turns (SPM p.76 row 97-98, 'a storm or environmental hazard'): a Strange Weather row (NCW p.3) that can blow in within the minutes of a gig: those lasting 1d6 x 10 minutes (radioactive windstorm, ash storm, deadly thunderstorm, dust storm) and the rains lasting 1d6 hours (acid, blood). HOUSE-RULE: the days-long rows (flooding, inversion smog, cold snap, heat wave, blackout) don't turn mid-gig; the twist rolls the pool evenly, never the weather it already has.

clear.name: Clear
clear._why: The neon-noir night as the game has always looked: violet smog lit pink and orange from below. Changes nothing.

overcast.name: Overcast
overcast.book: Overcast (NCW p.3); CPR core p.388: most days grim, gloomy and overcast
overcast._why: Low cloud over the city: no sun, no stars, the cloud's underside lit by the neon at night, flat grey by day.

drizzle.name: Light rain
drizzle.book: Light Rain/Sleet (NCW p.3, p.5: no visibility loss; slick surfaces)
drizzle._why: The cyberpunk classic: fine rain, the streets running wet with neon.

heavy_rain.name: Heavy rain
heavy_rain.book: Heavy Rain/Sleet (NCW p.3, p.5: -2 to see and to hit at a distance)
heavy_rain._why: A downpour: dense slanting rain, standing water, the far blocks lost in spray.

storm.name: Thunderstorm
storm.book: Deadly Thunderstorm (NCW p.3: 1d6 x 10 min; p.5: lightning, -2 to see and to hit at a distance); NC2045 p.16: two or three a year
storm._why: One of the city's rare, violent storms: driving rain, lightning flashing on the wet streets.

acid_rain.name: Acid rain
acid_rain.book: Acid Rain (NCW p.3: 1d6 hours; p.4: worn armor ablates 1 SP per full minute unprotected); CPR core p.244: periodic acid rainstorms
acid_rain._why: Chemical rain off the bay: sickly green streaks, wet glass, the far city sunk in green. RAW its harm takes a full minute out in it (20 rounds); the game leaves that out.

blood_rain.name: Blood rain
blood_rain.book: Blood Rain (NCW p.3: 1d6 hours; p.4: acid or biotoxin, -1 to see and to hit at a distance)
blood_rain._why: Greasy, pinkish-red rain from the 4th Corporate War's leftovers: red streaks, a rust-red sky. Its poison takes minutes out in it; the game keeps the -1.

ash.name: Ash storm
ash.book: Ash Storm (NCW p.3: 1d6 x 10 min; p.4: poison after a minute without a filter, -2 to see and to hit at a distance)
ash._why: Ash from the fires up north drifting down like grey snow, the far fires glowing on the horizon. Its poison takes a minute unmasked; the game keeps the -2.

dust.name: Dust storm
dust.book: Dust Storm (NCW p.3: 1d6 x 10 min; p.5: lungs clog after five minutes unmasked, -2 to see and to hit at a distance)
dust._why: Badlands dust blown in over the city: brown-orange haze, grit streaming down the street, a warm cast on everything far.

rad_wind.name: Radioactive windstorm
rad_wind.book: Radioactive Windstorm (NCW p.3: 1d6 x 10 min; p.5: bursts of high-level radiation off the Hot Zone, at the GM's discretion)
rad_wind._why: Wind off the Hot Zone carrying its dust: faintly glowing yellow-green grit gusting through, a sickly sky. The radiation bursts are the GM's call; the game leaves them out.

smog.name: Inversion smog
smog.book: Inversion Smog (NCW p.3: 1d6 days; p.5: thick as pea soup, poison after a minute unmasked, -4 to see and to hit at a distance); CPR core p.244: choking poison ground smog
smog._why: An inversion traps the factories' smog at street level: thick grey-yellow haze, the neon a dull glow through it. Its poison takes a minute unmasked; the game keeps the -4.

heat_wave.name: Heat wave
heat_wave.book: Heat Wave (NCW p.3: 1d6 days; p.5: armor penalties to REF, DEX and MOVE 2 worse)
heat_wave._why: The city cooking in the 110s: a bleached, hazy sky by day, a warm brown murk by night, the air shimmering over the asphalt.

cold_snap.name: Cold snap
cold_snap.book: Cold Snap (NCW p.3: 1d6 days; p.4: below freezing, black ice everywhere)
cold_snap._why: Below freezing: black ice on the streets, frost on the ground, ice crystals glittering in the lamp light, a hard blue sky. Icy footing is the GM's call; the game leaves it out.

flood.name: Flooding
flood.book: Flooding (NCW p.3: 1d6 days; p.5: a few inches at street level, a nuisance; basements and tunnels can fill)
flood._why: Sea water up through the cracked fill: the street under a few inches of black water, overcast above. A nuisance at street level; the game doesn't flood basements.

blackout.name: Blackout
blackout.book: Blackout (NCW p.3: 1d6 days; p.4: storm-felled power over 1d10 blocks: no power without a generator, no calls)
blackout._why: The storm took the grid down: the power is out (the Utility Codes' power outage: lights, cameras and turrets dead), the sky over the dark blocks unlit.

weights._why: In 1/1440ths of the base (the year-round Night City Weather odds, NCW p.3; see _doc). Leanings add to it.

region._why: HOUSE-RULE: the Outskirts are the Badlands' edge, where the dust storms come from (NC2045 p.297: pollutant-carrying dust storms regularly sweep through).

profile._why: HOUSE-RULE: the Hot Zone's radioactive dust is what the windstorms carry (NCW p.5); the corporate centre's and the Exec Zone's air is scrubbed (no source: kept small).

look._why: Each district's look tags (docs/world): 'yellow smog' is the Heywood Industrial Zone, where most days a thick yellow smog blankets everything (NC2045 p.256): about half its gigs. The rest are HOUSE-RULE leanings, small beside the base.
